# The PUBLIC developer API surface, one `METHOD /path` per line.
#
# This file is the reviewed answer to "what can an API key reach?".
# .github/workflows/scripts/api_contract.py diffs it against the operations in
# the generated public OpenAPI document on every commit, and any difference —
# in either direction — is a red build. That is the whole point: a route
# appears on the public surface only when somebody edits this file in the same
# commit and a reviewer reads the line.
#
# Taken verbatim from docs/developer-platform/CONTRACT.md §7 on 2026-09-12,
# before orchestrator/app/publicapi/ existed. Until that package lands the
# gate reports "not enforced yet" and passes; after it lands, this list is
# binding with no further edit to the pipeline.
#
# What is DELIBERATELY absent, per CONTRACT-3 §7: Salesforce, RAG and web
# search, deep research, uploads, artifacts, memory, conversation history and
# admin analytics. Each would need its own product, scope and threat review,
# so each must arrive here as its own reviewed line, never as a side effect of
# mounting a router.
#
# Comments (`#`) and blank lines are ignored. Order does not matter; the
# comparison is on sets.

# ---- models: only the models this key may use (CONTRACT-3 §7, §15) --------
GET /v1/models
GET /v1/models/{model}

# ---- responses: the one generation path (§8, §11) ------------------------
# Sync, streaming and background all arrive through POST /v1/responses; the
# background and cancel routes are how a client that disconnected catches up.
POST /v1/responses
GET /v1/responses/{id}
POST /v1/responses/{id}/cancel

# ---- compatibility shape, same engine path (§7) --------------------------
POST /v1/chat/completions

# ---- usage: project-scoped, bounded range (§7) ---------------------------
GET /v1/usage

# ---- the schema itself (§7: "the public schema only") --------------------
# If the document deliberately does not describe its own schema endpoint,
# delete this line and say so in the commit message — a considered decision is
# exactly what this file is for. Do not "fix" the red build by loosening the
# comparison.
GET /v1/openapi.json
